learn: The elements of art are the building blocks artists use: line, shape, form, colour, value, texture and space.
Line is a moving dot. Shape is a flat enclosed area. Form is three-dimensional.
Every artwork uses several elements together.
check: How many elements of art are there?
lessons.try: Find an artwork online and name three elements you see.

learn: Colour comes from light. It has a name, like blue, called its hue.
Value is how light or dark something is.
Texture is how something feels or looks like it feels.
check: The name of a colour is its...
Feels or looks like it feels
lessons.try: Make a value scale of five squares from white to black.

learn: Space is the area around, between and within objects.
Positive space is filled by objects. Negative space is the empty area.
Artists use space to show depth and to give the eye room to rest.
check: The empty area around objects is...
lessons.try: Draw a chair by only drawing the spaces between its legs.

learn: A value scale shows steps from lightest to darkest.
Highlights are the lightest areas, where light hits most directly.
Shadows are the darkest areas, away from the light.
lessons.try: Create a nine-step value scale with a pencil.

learn: Blending makes smooth changes from light to dark.
Hatching and cross-hatching use lines to build darkness.
Stippling uses dots. Closer dots look darker.
check: Smooth changes from light to dark is...
lessons.try: Shade a sphere using blending, then another using cross-hatching.

learn: A cast shadow is the shadow an object throws onto a surface.
It falls on the opposite side from the light source.
Cast shadows make objects look like they sit on the ground.
check: Like they sit on the ground
The shadow an object throws on a surface
lessons.try: Set an apple near a lamp and draw it with its cast shadow.

learn: A monochromatic scheme uses one hue with its tints and shades.
Picasso's Blue Period paintings (1901-1904) mostly used blues.
Monochromatic art can feel calm and unified.
lessons.try: Paint a landscape in only one colour plus white and black.

learn: Analogous colours sit next to each other on the wheel, like yellow, yellow-orange and orange.
Complementary colours sit opposite, like blue and orange.
Complementary colours make each other look brighter.
check: Complementary colours make each other look...
lessons.try: Make two small paintings: one analogous, one complementary.

learn: Neutral colours are black, white, grey and brown.
Neutrals can make bright colours stand out.
Artists choose a scheme to match the mood they want.
check: Artists choose a colour scheme to match...
lessons.try: Paint a single bright flower on a neutral background.

learn: A landscape has three areas: foreground (closest), middle ground and background (farthest).
Foreground objects are larger and more detailed. Background objects are smaller and paler.
Overlapping also shows depth.
check: The area closest to the viewer is the...
lessons.try: Draw a landscape with something in each of the three grounds.

learn: Far-away objects look bluer, lighter and less detailed because of the air between us and them.
This is called atmospheric perspective.
Leonardo da Vinci used it in his landscapes.
lessons.try: Paint three rows of mountains getting lighter and bluer as they go back.

learn: One-point perspective uses a horizon line and one vanishing point.
Lines going away from you, like road edges, meet at the vanishing point.
It makes roads, hallways and railway tracks look deep.
check: Lines going away meet at the...
One-point perspective uses how many vanishing points?
Which looks deep with one-point perspective?
lessons.try: Draw a road disappearing into the distance using a vanishing point.

learn: The principles of design tell how artists arrange the elements.
Symmetrical balance is the same on both sides, like a butterfly.
Asymmetrical balance uses different things that feel equally weighted, like a large shape balanced by several small ones.
check: Principles of design tell how artists...
lessons.try: Make one symmetrical and one asymmetrical design.

learn: Emphasis is making one part stand out as the focal point.
Contrast, like bright against dull or big against small, creates emphasis.
The viewer's eye goes to the focal point first.
check: The part that stands out most
Where does the eye go first?
lessons.try: Draw a crowd of grey circles with one bright red circle.

learn: Rhythm is created by repeating elements, like a beat in music.
Movement guides the viewer's eye through the artwork.
Unity is the feeling that all parts belong together.
check: Rhythm in art is made by...
lessons.try: Create a design where wavy lines lead the eye to a focal point.

learn: Collage became an art form in the early 1900s when Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque glued paper into paintings.
Later, Henri Matisse made huge collages of painted, cut paper.
Collage uses paper, photos, fabric and found materials.
check: Who glued paper into paintings in the early 1900s?
lessons.try: Make a collage using at least three different papers.

learn: Arrange pieces before gluing to try different compositions.
Use the principles of design: balance, emphasis and unity.
Layer pieces from background to foreground.
lessons.try: Arrange a collage three ways and photograph each before choosing.

learn: Mixed media combines different materials, like paint, ink, collage and drawing.
Artists can draw on top of collage or paint over textures.
Experimenting leads to surprising results.
check: Can artists draw on top of collage?
lessons.try: Create a mixed media piece using paint, paper and pencil.

learn: Eyes are halfway between the top of the head and the chin.
The space between the eyes is about one eye width.
The bottom of the nose is halfway between the eyes and chin, and the mouth is a third of the way below the nose.
check: The space between the eyes is about...
The bottom of the nose is...
lessons.try: Draw a face using proportion guidelines.

learn: Facial expressions show feelings.
Eyebrows, eyes and mouth change shape with emotions.
Raised eyebrows can show surprise; a furrowed brow can show worry.
lessons.try: Draw the same face with three different expressions.

learn: Leonardo da Vinci painted the "Mona Lisa" in the early 1500s, famous for her mysterious smile.
Frida Kahlo painted many self-portraits showing her life and Mexican heritage.
Portraits tell us about the person and the time they lived in.
lessons.try: Create a self-portrait that includes symbols of things you love.

learn: In relief printing, you carve away parts you don't want to print. Raised parts hold ink.
Linocuts and woodcuts are types of relief prints.
Japanese artist Katsushika Hokusai made the famous woodblock print "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" around 1831.
check: Who made "The Great Wave off Kanagawa"?
lessons.try: Carve a design into a foam plate and print it.

learn: Prints come out as mirror images, so letters must be carved backwards.
Registration means lining up the paper the same way each time.
Good registration helps when printing more than one colour.
check: Lining up the paper each time
lessons.try: Write your name backwards on a foam plate and print it.

learn: A reduction print carves more away after each colour.
Print the lightest colour first, then darker colours on top.
Each layer adds detail.
check: In a reduction print, after each colour you...
lessons.try: Make a two-colour print: light colour first, carve more, then dark colour.

learn: Pinch pots are made by pinching a ball of clay into a bowl.
Coil pots are built by stacking ropes of clay.
Slab construction uses flat sheets of clay joined together.
check: Stacking ropes of clay makes a...
A pinch pot starts as a...
lessons.try: Make a small coil pot.

learn: To join clay, score (scratch) both surfaces and add slip (watery clay).
Press together and smooth the seam.
Poorly joined pieces can crack or fall off when drying.
lessons.try: Add a handle to a pinch pot using score and slip.

learn: Clay dries to a hard state called greenware.
A kiln fires clay at very high heat to make it permanent. Only adults operate kilns.
Glaze is a glassy coating applied before a second firing.
lessons.try: Design the glaze colours you would use on your pot (on paper).

learn: Ancient Greeks made marble statues and painted pottery with black and red figures.
Ancient Chinese artists made bronze vessels and later, around 210 BCE, the Terracotta Army of thousands of clay soldiers.
Mayan artists carved stone stelae and painted murals.
check: The Terracotta Army is made of...
lessons.try: Design a Greek-style pot with a story painted on it.

learn: An art movement is a group of artists with a shared style at a time.
Impressionists, like Claude Monet in the 1870s, painted light and colour with quick brushstrokes.
Cubists, like Picasso, showed objects from many angles at once.
lessons.try: Paint a view out of a window in Impressionist style with quick dabs.

learn: Art critics describe, analyse, interpret and judge.
Describe what you see. Analyse how elements and principles are used.
Interpret what it means, then judge whether it is successful and why.
check: What is the first step of a critique?
How elements and principles are used
lessons.try: Write a four-step critique of a famous painting.
